text:
maria_support: Heads-up — Peregrine (dp-78) hit persistent 429s during their promo blast yesterday morning. They report baseline ~120 qps, sustained peak ~720 qps for ~15–25m and the pool reported ~95% GPU util. Autoscale didn't add nodes.
jon_sre: :eyes: Do we have timeline + sample request IDs from them? Also which autoscale policy is attached to dp-78?
maria_support: Sent their logs. Root ts 2026-03-16T08:12:03Z. Example error payload they sent: `{"error":"rate_limit","message":"dedicated capacity throttled"}`. They included X-Request-Id headers: `req-8f3a0b` and `req-8f3a11`.
nadia_eng: Looking at dp-78 config — policy uses target_util=0.7 with 60s cooldown, scale_step=1. If baseline bursts quickly to 6x baseline, 60s cooldown + conservative step can under-react.
lee_account: Peregrine is on a committed monthly reservation but didn't buy burst credits. They're sensitive to throttles because of SLA with their client.
jon_sre: Can you paste short metric snippets? GPU mem and nvlink?
maria_support: From their telemetry (approx): `2026-03-16 08:10 GPU0 util 92%, GPU1 util 94%, batch queue length 48, avg latency 420ms`, then at 08:15 we see `429 spike ~2200 requests/min` for ~18m.
nadia_eng: That queue length + high util says model runtime saturated. Two paths: (A) immediate mitigation — increase pool size by +2 GPUs and enable burst capacity, (B) longer term — lower per-request concurrency / shorter timeouts or add autoscale policy with larger step and 15s eval window.
jon_sre: Could be noisy neighbor? Any other tenants on dp-78?
maria_support: dp-78 is shared across 3 small customers by default. Peregrine has the majority of traffic during campaign window but not exclusive.
jon_sre: Share noisy neighbor repro: ask Peregrine to run a controlled load with `ab` or our `ri-load` script against their route so we can reproduce in our environment. Send exact curl they used.
maria_support: They provided a sample curl they used to hit endpoint: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hello","max_tokens":256}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -i``` They included failing response headers: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, `X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-Redwood-Pool: dp-78`.
lee_account: Recommend we offer immediate temporary dedicated bump (2 GPUs) + waive burst fees for this campaign window. Want to confirm cost impact before proposing.
nadia_eng: For ops: change autoscale policy on dp-78 to `evaluation_window=15s, scale_step=2, max_extra=4` and enable prefix cache to reduce load. Also add a short-term rule: if GPU util >= 90% for 30s -> scale +2.
jon_sre: I'll queue a hotfix for the autoscaler and run a canary scale on a staging twin pool first, then apply to dp-78 if metrics look good. ETA 20m.
autoscale-bot: [autoscale] policy-change-request created by jon_sre for dp-78 (change id: acr-20260316-22).
maria_support: Informing Peregrine that we are applying an emergency scale + policy tweak. Also asked them for a reproducible load test window 30m from now.
lee_account: I started a billing exception draft for waiving burst overage for yesterday's window; will loop in finance.
jon_sre: Post-action checklist: 1) apply policy tweak 2) scale +2 GPUs 3) monitor 5m windows for queue length/429s 4) if still present escalate to engineering.
maria_support: Peregrine confirmed a scheduled load window at 08:50 UTC. I'll have them share request-ids.
nadia_eng: For long-term, propose we offer them a dedicated-only tenancy option or recommend reservation with burst credits and a higher target_util (0.75->0.85) for marketing spikes.
jon_sre: Agreed. Captured runbook steps in ticket RI-4521.
maria_support: Thanks team — will post update after the canary scale. :thumbsup:
lee_account: I'll wait for final metrics before sending customer PO for permanent resizing. :ok_hand:
